'''Michel Xavier Goemans''' (born December 1964) is a [[Belgium|Belgian]]-[[United States|American]] [[professor]] of [[applied mathematics]] and the RSA Professor of Mathematics at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] working in [[discrete mathematics]] and [[combinatorial optimization]] at [[CSAIL]] and MIT Operations Research Center.<ref>{{Cite web|title=School of Science appoints 11 faculty members to named professorships|url=https://news.mit.edu/2021/school-science-appoints-faculty-named-professorships-1101|access-date=2021-11-03|website=MIT News {{!}} [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] |date=November 2021 |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==
Goemans earned his doctorate in 1990 from MIT.<ref name="mathgene"/> Goemans is the "Leighton Family Professor" of Applied Mathematics at MIT and an adjunct professor at the [[University of Waterloo]]. He was also a professor at the [[University of Louvain]] and a visiting professor at the [[Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences|RIMS]] of the [[University of Kyoto]].

==Recognition==
In 1991 he received the [[Tucker Prize|A.W. Tucker Prize]]. From 1995 to 1997 he was a [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Sloan Research Fellow]]. In 1998 he was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite book|author=Goemans, Michel X.|chapter=Semidefinite programming and combinatorial optimization|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. III|year=1998|pages=657–666|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011620000}}</ref> For the academic year 2007–2008 he [[Guggenheim Fellow]].

Goemans is a [[List of Fellows of the Association for Computing Machinery|Fellow of the Association for Computing Machinery]] (2008),<ref>[http://awards.acm.org/award_winners/goemans_4568770.cfm Michel Goemans, ACM Fellows, United States 2008], retrieved 2015-10-19</ref> a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (2012),<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-01-19.</ref> and a fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (2013).<ref>[http://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=year&value=2013 SIAM Fellows: Class of 2013], retrieved 2015-10-19.</ref> In 2000 he was awarded the MOS-AMS [[Fulkerson Prize]]<ref>[http://www.mathopt.org/?nav=fulkerson#winners Past Winners of the Fulkerson Prize], retrieved 2015-10-19.</ref> for joint work with [[David P. Williamson]] on the [[semidefinite programming]] approximation algorithm for the [[maximum cut]] problem. In 2012 Goemans was awarded the Farkas Prize.<ref>{{cite web|title=Michel Goemans is selected as the winner of the 2012 INFORMS Optimization Society Farkas Prize|website=informs.org|url=https://connect.informs.org/optimizationsociety/prizes/farkas-prize/2012}}</ref> In 2022 he received the [[Leroy P. Steele Prize|AMS Steele Prize for Seminal Contribution to Research]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/news?news_id=6893 AMS Steele Prize for Seminal Contribution to Research 2022]</ref>

==Personal life==
His hobby is sailing. Goemans has Belgian and US citizenship.<ref>{{cite web |title=Michel Goemans - Bio |url=https://math.mit.edu/~goemans/bio.html |website=math.mit.edu |access-date=17 November 2025|quote=American & Belgian citizen, born December 1964. Enjoys sailing.}}</ref>
